<a id="layout"></a>
## Share the layout, not a guessed character width

Click the paragraph to place a marker at the nearest shaped cluster index.
[`StyledText::layout`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/struct.StyledText.html#method.layout) returns a shared [`TextLayout`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/struct.TextLayout.html). Cloning it lets the
input handler and marker query the same shaped geometry the text element
measured. Position queries need layout and prepaint to have populated that
geometry; building the element tree is too early.

The paragraph container uses `.flex().flex_col()` so the text is measured
as its own child. A block div instead gathers text into a shared paragraph;
that paragraph owns the geometry and leaves this handle unpopulated. The
text still wraps within its 280-pixel width in the flex container.

The string includes a combining accent in `Café` and a multibyte `ß`.
Neither a Rust `char` count nor a fixed character width can locate every
displayed cluster. Change the paragraph width and try the wrapped lines.

```rust
use gpui::{
    AppContext, Bounds, Context, IntoElement, MouseButton, MouseDownEvent, Render, Role,
    StyledText, TextLayout, Window, canvas, div, fill, prelude::*, px, rgb, size, text,
};

const PARAGRAPH: &str = "Café — Straße — click a wrapped line to inspect its UTF-8 byte index.";

struct HitTest {
    index: usize,
    hit: bool,
}

fn component(_window: &mut Window, cx: &mut gpui::App) -> gpui::Entity<HitTest> {
    cx.new(|_cx| HitTest {
        index: 0,
        hit: false,
    })
}
```

<a id="hit"></a>
## Keep the hit and the nearest edge distinct

[`TextLayout::index_for_position`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/struct.TextLayout.html#method.index_for_position) returns `Ok(index)` for a hit on text and
`Err(index)` for the nearest visual edge when the position is outside a line.
Both are UTF-8 byte offsets. The handler keeps the hit/edge distinction in
its status and calls [`Context::notify`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/struct.Context.html#method.notify) so the marker is rendered again.

This demonstrates a cluster marker. A text editor also needs caret affinity,
grapheme-aware movement, selection, focus, and input-method handling. See
the [text guide](@/guides/text.md) before building those on a display element.
The paragraph has an accessible text label and the byte report uses [`text`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/macro.text.html).
Moving this diagnostic marker remains a pointer-only operation; it is not a
keyboard-accessible text selection control.

```rust
impl Render for HitTest {
    fn render(&mut self, _window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        let text = StyledText::new(PARAGRAPH);
        let input_layout = text.layout().clone();
        let marker_layout = text.layout().clone();
        let index = self.index;
        div()
            .size_full()
            .flex()
            .flex_col()
            .items_center()
            .justify_center()
            .gap_4()
            .bg(rgb(0xf7f6f2))
            .text_color(rgb(0x202b29))
            .child(
                div()
                    .id("paragraph")
                    .role(Role::Label)
                    .aria_label(PARAGRAPH)
                    .relative()
                    .flex()
                    .flex_col()
                    .w(px(280.))
                    .text_size(px(18.))
                    .line_height(px(28.))
                    .cursor_text()
                    .on_mouse_down(
                        MouseButton::Left,
                        cx.listener(move |this, event: &MouseDownEvent, _window, cx| {
                            let result = input_layout.index_for_position(event.position);
                            this.hit = result.is_ok();
                            this.index = result.unwrap_or_else(|edge| edge);
                            cx.notify();
                        }),
                    )
                    .child(text)
                    .child(marker(marker_layout, index)),
            )
            .child(text!(format!(
                "Byte {} / {} · {}",
                self.index,
                PARAGRAPH.len(),
                if self.hit {
                    "cluster hit"
                } else {
                    "visual edge"
                },
            )))
    }
}
```

<a id="marker"></a>
## Map the index back after prepaint

The [`canvas`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/fn.canvas.html) runs after the paragraph's text child. Its prepaint callback
asks [`TextLayout::position_for_index`](https://docs.rs/gpui-ce/0.2.2/gpui/struct.TextLayout.html#method.position_for_index) for the marker's window-space point;
paint uses that point directly. Subtract the text bounds only if the caller
needs local coordinates. No extra offset belongs in this paint call.

At a soft wrap, the following line owns the boundary position. A byte inside
an atomic shaping cluster maps to its logical start, so adjacent visible
glyphs need not have adjacent byte indices. Click at the start of the next
wrapped line and compare the displayed byte offset with the marker position.

```rust
fn marker(layout: TextLayout, index: usize) -> impl IntoElement {
    canvas(
        move |_bounds, _window, _cx| {
            // The preceding text child has already completed prepaint.
            (layout.position_for_index(index), layout.line_height())
        },
        |_bounds, (position, height), window, _cx| {
            if let Some(position) = position {
                window.paint_quad(fill(
                    Bounds::new(position, size(px(2.), height)),
                    rgb(0xd04736),
                ));
            }
        },
    )
    .absolute()
    .inset_0()
}

pub fn main() {
    support::run(component);
}
```
